security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives in a Markdown-only REST API guide. The backtick findings are code fences or endpoint examples, the API key finding is a placeholder example, and the blocker findings are normal API documentation. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Example API keys resemble live credential formats.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sk_live_abc123 with clearly non-secret placeholders such as EXAMPLE_API_KEY in every example.

remediation.issue: Many Markdown code fences trigger simplistic command-execution detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that all blocks are documentation examples and are not commands to execute.

422 Unprocessable   - Valid syntax but semantic error

content.value_statement: Inconsistent APIs slow integration and create client errors. This skill provides practical REST guidance for resources, methods, responses, errors, pagination, versioning, authentication, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Defines resource-oriented URL patterns using plural nouns and shallow hierarchy.
Maps HTTP methods to common create, read, update, and delete operations.
Recommends consistent response, error, naming, pagination, filtering, and sorting patterns.
Explains status code choices for success, client error, and server error cases.
Covers versioning, authentication examples, rate-limit headers, and OpenAPI documentation basics.
limitations: Focuses on REST APIs and does not cover GraphQL, gRPC, or event-driven contracts.
Provides design guidance, not a framework, generator, linter, or test suite.
Uses short examples that may need adaptation for domain-specific authorization and compliance requirements.
Does not validate an existing OpenAPI document automatically.

use_cases.title: Plan a New REST API
use_cases.description: Create a consistent endpoint structure before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Review Endpoint Consistency
use_cases.description: Compare proposed routes, status codes, and response shapes against practical REST conventions.

use_cases.title: Standardize API Documentation
use_cases.description: Prepare endpoint documentation with request parameters, response schemas, examples, and error cases.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Endpoints
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small resource model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design REST endpoints for these resources: [resources]. Include URL patterns, HTTP methods, and expected success status codes.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize Existing Routes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of inconsistent endpoint names.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these API routes for REST consistency: [routes]. Suggest resource-based alternatives and explain each change briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Design Responses and Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate work on client-facing response contracts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Define response and error patterns for this endpoint: [endpoint]. Include success cases, validation errors, authorization errors, and pagination if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an API Contract
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before implementation or public release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this API design for consistency, versioning, pagination, authentication, rate limiting, and documentation gaps: [api summary]. Prioritize the highest-impact fixes.

output_examples.input: Design user and order endpoints for a commerce service.
output_examples.output: A resource map with users and orders, recommended methods, nested relationship guidance, status code choices, and pagination notes.

output_examples.input: Review routes that use action names like getUser and createOrder.
output_examples.output: A route review that replaces action verbs with plural resources and explains which HTTP method should express each action.

output_examples.input: Prepare documentation requirements for a create-user endpoint.
output_examples.output: A documentation checklist covering request fields, response shape, validation errors, authentication, rate limits, and example scenarios.

best_practices: Start with resources and relationships before choosing endpoint names.
Use consistent response shapes and status codes across the whole API.
Document authentication, errors, rate limits, pagination, and versioning before release.
anti_patterns: Do not put action verbs such as get or create into REST resource URLs.
Do not expose internal data models directly in public responses.
Do not skip pagination or rate limiting for collection endpoints.

faq.question: Does this skill generate production API code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and review criteria for REST APIs.

faq.question: Can it help with OpenAPI documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a documentation checklist and a small OpenAPI-style example.

faq.question: Does it support GraphQL or gRPC design?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is focused on REST API conventions.

faq.question: Can it review existing endpoint names?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare routes against resource naming, method usage, and consistency rules.

faq.question: Does it cover API security?
faq.answer: It covers authentication placement, rate limiting, and avoiding internal data exposure at a design level.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Backend engineers, API reviewers, and technical writers can use it to make REST APIs more consistent.
